title: Vendor names on the command line: Claude is refused, claude works
lead: *Proposed.* `--implementer Claude:sonnet:high` (and `--reviewer`, `--architect`, `ork vendor out Claude`) is refused as an unsupported vendor, while `claude:sonnet:high` works, and the error does not list the valid names. This slice makes vendor names case-insensitive and normalised, or makes the error list the vendors and suggest the lowercase spelling, or both. Which one, and in which layer, is open: see `Open owner questions`.
findings_note: Owner 2026-11-04: ork wave start ... --implementer Claude:sonnet:high is refused as unsupported vendor; claude:sonnet:high works. The daemon matches vendors exactly (runner.go:90, runs.go:471-474) while matrix rows are matched case-insensitively (runs.go:428).
boundary: **Not in this slice:** model and effort spelling (passed to the vendor CLIs as given; not checked here); aliases such as the matrix's `Claude Code` on the command line (Q3); new vendors.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Owner evidence, 2026-11-04: `ork wave start ... --implementer Claude:sonnet:high` was rejected with "unsupported vendor", and the lowercase spelling worked.

What the code at HEAD of main shows (read 2026-11-04):

- `lineupFlags.apply` (`internal/cli/lineup.go:36-77`) splits `VENDOR:MODEL:EFFORT` at the first and last colon (`:59-67`) and keeps the vendor as typed. The CLI does not check it.
- The daemon checks it: planRun returns `bad params: unsupported vendor %q for %s` when supportsVendor fails (`internal/daemon/runs.go:471-474`). `supportsVendor` is an exact match on `claude`, `codex` or `grok` (`internal/daemon/runner.go:90`). The error does not list them. `TestRunPlanRefusesBadOverride` (`internal/daemon/runs_test.go:398`) has the case "unsupported vendor" with `acme`.
- `ork vendor out|back NAME` matches exactly against `vendorNames` (`internal/cli/vendor.go:16`, `:76-78`). Its error does list them: "unsupported vendor %q; use claude, codex or grok". The daemon's vendor.set handler also lists them (`internal/daemon/vendors.go:60`).
- The matrix path is already case-insensitive: `matrixAdapters[strings.ToLower(row.Agent)]` (`internal/daemon/runs.go:348`, `:428`, `:447`; `internal/daemon/matrix.go:76`; `internal/daemon/speccheck.go:115`), where a matrix agent `Claude Code` maps to `claude`. So the plan shows lineups taken from rows named `Claude Code`, while the flag needs `claude`.
- The engine and runners compare vendors exactly (`internal/daemon/runner.go:29`, `:92-98`; `internal/engine/brief.go:98`; `internal/engine/round.go:51`). So a non-normalised name must not reach them; normalising at the edge (CLI and wire) is enough.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/cli/lineup.go:59-67` (normalise or check the vendor of each entry).
- `internal/cli/vendor.go:16` and `:76-78` (`vendor out|back`).
- `internal/daemon/runs.go:471-474` (normalise the wire's lineup entries before `supportsVendor`, and list the vendors in the error) and `internal/daemon/runner.go:90`.
- `internal/daemon/vendors.go:60` (`vendor.set`).
- `internal/cli/run_test.go` (beside `TestRunLineupFlagUsageErrors` at `:614` and `TestLineupErrorsNameCommandAndFlags` at `:635`), `TestWaveStartLineupFlagsApplyToEveryItem` (`internal/cli/wave_test.go:447`), `TestVendorCommandUsageErrors` (`internal/cli/vendor_test.go:100`), `internal/daemon/runs_test.go:398`.
- `docs/guide.md:196-205` (the lineup flags) and `docs/design.md:1189` (CLI).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
Under Q1 options 1 and 3:

- `TestLineupVendorIsCaseInsensitive` (`internal/cli/run_test.go`): for `run p S1` and `wave start p S1 S2`, each of `Claude:sonnet:high`, `CLAUDE:sonnet:high`, `Codex:gpt-5:high` and `GROK:latest:high` in `--implementer`, `--reviewer` and `--architect` sends the lineup with vendor `claude`, `codex` or `grok` (lowercase) to `run.plan` and `run.start`; model and effort are sent as typed. Fails first: the vendor is sent as typed.
- `TestRunPlanNormalisesVendorCase` (`internal/daemon/runs_test.go`): a `run.plan` wire lineup with vendor `Claude` plans with `claude`. Fails first: "unsupported vendor \"Claude\"".
- `TestVendorOutIsCaseInsensitive` (`internal/cli/vendor_test.go`): `ork vendor out Claude` sends `claude`. Fails first: "unsupported vendor \"Claude\"".

Under Q1 options 2 and 3:

- `TestUnknownLineupVendorListsTheVendors` (`internal/cli/run_test.go`): `--implementer acme:m:high` exits 2 with "ork: run: --implementer: unsupported vendor \"acme\"; use claude, codex or grok", before any daemon call. Fails first: the daemon's error, without the list.
- `TestRunPlanUnsupportedVendorListsTheVendors` (`internal/daemon/runs_test.go`): the `acme` case of `TestRunPlanRefusesBadOverride` says "use claude, codex or grok". Fails first: no list.
- Under Q1 option 2 only: `TestMixedCaseVendorSuggestsLowercase`: `--implementer Claude:sonnet:high` exits 2 with `did you mean "claude"?`. Fails first: no suggestion.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Tests first. Confirm each fails for the reason given.
2. One place for the names: export the list from `internal/daemon` (for example `daemon.Vendors()`, used by `supportsVendor`, `vendor.set` and `internal/cli/vendor.go`). Drop the CLI's second copy, `vendorNames` (`internal/cli/vendor.go:16`).
3. Q1 option 1 or 3: `strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(v))` on the vendor in `lineupFlags.apply`, in `vendor out|back`, and on every lineup entry of the `run.plan` / `run.start` wire in `planRun` before the check. The engine and run record see only lowercase names.
4. Q1 option 2 or 3: the CLI checks the vendor in `apply` and fails with the listed vendors (`vendorList()`). The daemon error lists them too.
5. Update `docs/guide.md` (the lineup flags: vendor names are case-insensitive, or must be lowercase) in the same diff.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go -C WORKTREE test -count=1 ./internal/cli ./internal/daemon -run 'Vendor|Lineup|BadOverride'`: all pass.
- `go -C WORKTREE test -race -count=1 ./...`, `go -C WORKTREE vet ./...`, `gofmt -l WORKTREE` (empty), `slicer check`, `adj lint`.
- Mutation: remove the lowercase step in `planRun`; `TestRunPlanNormalisesVendorCase` goes red.
- [HUMAN CHECK] `ork run P ID --implementer Claude:sonnet:high` shows a plan whose implementer row reads `claude`.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch: "Vendor names are case-insensitive; errors list the vendors".

sections.heading: Open owner questions
sections.body:
UI slice by rule u10 (`internal/cli` output), so it gets a UI pass.

Question: How should ork treat a vendor name in another case, such as Claude?
Options:
1. normalise: accept any case and store lowercase
2. strict-hint: refuse it, list the vendors and suggest the lowercase spelling
3. both: accept any case, and for an unknown name list the vendors
Recommend: 3 - the matrix already reads agent names case-insensitively, and a typo still gets a clear list

Question: Where should the normalising and the check happen?
Options:
1. cli-and-daemon: the CLI for an early error and the daemon on the wire, so the TUI and any client agree
2. cli-only: the daemon stays exact
Recommend: 1 - the daemon is the one place every client passes, and the CLI check saves a round trip

Question: Should the command line also accept the matrix agent names, such as Claude Code?
Options:
1. no: only claude, codex and grok
2. yes: map the matrix names on the command line too
Recommend: 1 - the flag form VENDOR:MODEL:EFFORT has no room for spaces, and no one has asked for it
